findings.evidence: plugins/specflow/skills/complete/SKILL.md:358-377 — Phase G (Linear status sync) is a 19-line phase whose entire body covers Linear MCP detection, transition firing, and ambiguous-merge-state skip. The phase traces in the SKILL header `produces:` block to no PRD requirement explicitly (R1-R14 do not name Linear sync; AC-1 through AC-15 do not name Linear transitions). The PRD's See-also (line 188 of PRD) lists `skills/develop/SKILL.md` Phase F.4 firing 'In Progress → In Review', and the SKILL body at line 370 says '`specflow:develop` Phase F.4 fires `In Progress → In Review`; the human merge fires `In Review → Done` typically. The retro skill's `Done` transition is the **post-merge** semantic'. So the SKILL body added a Linear sync phase that the PRD does not anchor to any R or AC. Reverse traceability lens (per E4 prompt edit calibration anchor — Gate 2 002-develop-skill goal-r1-f1): every phase should trace to ≥1 R or AC. Phase G traces to 'cross-skill integration with `specflow:develop`' but no R-level requirement establishes that contract.
findings.claim: Reverse-traceability gap (orphan phase) — Phase G (Linear status sync) has no R-anchor and no AC-anchor. The SKILL body justifies it on cross-skill consistency grounds (`specflow:develop` Phase F.4 fires the predecessor transition), but the PRD did not require this skill to fire the post-merge transition. Per the orphan-AC rule established at 002-develop-skill Gate 2 (goal-r1-f1) — every section should trace to a PRD anchor. Phase G is the Phase-3-retro version of the orphan pattern. The SKILL author may have inferred this phase from the calibration anchor's Linear pattern, but inference is not a substitute for PRD anchor.
findings.proposed_change: Either (a) drop Phase G entirely — defer the post-merge Linear transition to a future PRD enhancement (the SKILL would have 7 phases A-F, H instead of 8; the chat-line summary at H.2 already names 'Linear: synced|skipped|not-configured' so the Linear-state surface in user-visible output is preserved); OR (b) surface Phase G as a documented inferred-from-calibration choice with explicit PRD-Open-Question routing — flag in the SKILL body that Phase G is implementer-stated and should be ratified or dropped via PRD scope-change. Preference: (b) — the post-merge transition is consistent with the cross-skill ecosystem and dropping it would orphan the chat-line at H.2. The documented-inference path closes the traceability gap without a PRD revision.

findings.evidence: plugins/specflow/skills/complete/SKILL.md:266-270 — Phase E.3 (compute scope_change_log) handles a 'task dropped during scope-change' edge case by refusing with a literal sentinel and exiting. The branch is documented at T13 Notes as an implementer choice ('Branch (c) (task dropped by scope-change) is an implementation choice not directly named in PRD R13/AC-13'). The SKILL body inherits this branch but the verify steps at H.4 (lines 410-419) do not include a check that this refusal path emits the literal sentinel — H.4.4 says 'Chat-line summary OR one of the five sentinel failure lines was emitted', which does name E.3's sentinel as one of the five (per H.3 enumeration), but H.3 lists only five sentinels and the user might trace 'every refusal exits with a sentinel' to AC-15's binary check without realising the H.3 list is the verifier-binding source.
findings.claim: Coverage thread — every PRD R-ID maps to a section (forward coverage holds: R1→A.1, R2→A.1, R3→C.1+E.1, R4→B.3+E.5, R5→E.4, R6→D.1, R7→F.2-F.3, R8→Inputs/Anti-patterns, R9→B.4, R10→E.2, R11→D.2, R12→D.2+F.4, R13→E.3, R14→A.3). But the verify-step-binding for AC-15 (H.4.4) refers to 'one of the five sentinel failure lines' which counts five sentinels (A.1/A.2 combined, A.3, B.3, B.4, E.3) where the originally-natural enumeration would be six (treating A.1 and A.2 as separate). The collapse from six to five is correct (A.1 and A.2 share the auto-fire-precondition refusal pattern) but the asymmetry between the H.3 enumeration ('five refusal sentinel chat lines') and the AC-15 binding (verify-zero-silent-exits) deserves a one-line cross-reference so a Verifier reading H.4.4 cannot mis-bind.
findings.proposed_change: Add a one-line note at H.3 explicitly enumerating the five sentinel chat lines as a stable five-tuple consumed by H.4.4: '(1) auto-fire missing entry / Verifier reject; (2) concurrent-fire lock; (3) cross-skill schema unmet; (4) plain-mode existing-retro; (5) scope-changed task missing.' The list is already there — the addition is just numbering the five so H.4.4's reference is mechanical, not narrative. This closes the AC-15 verify-step-to-sentinel-list binding gap.
